### The Imperative for Edge AI in Field Epidemiology

In an increasingly interconnected global landscape, the threat of emerging infectious diseases and potential pandemics has never been higher. Modern societal expansion—driven by climate change, rapid urbanization, globalization, industrial livestock farming, and human encroachment into natural habitats—creates conditions of self-organized criticality. In this complex ecosystem, field epidemiology stands as the critical first line of defense against novel pathogens, mutated strains, and potential biosecurity threats. Yet, despite its essential role in safeguarding public health, field epidemiology remains significantly underserved by advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

### Operational Challenges in Public Health Infrastructure

Local health departments (LHDs) operate on the front lines of disease surveillance and outbreak response, but they frequently face severe systemic constraints. Most LHDs endure perpetual underfunding and chronic staffing shortages. Consequently, deploying complex cloud infrastructure, managing sophisticated model pipelines, or maintaining continuous subscription-based API services is practically impossible for these organizations.

Furthermore, epidemiologists work in the field under unpredictable conditions where high-speed internet connectivity is far from guaranteed. The data gathered during investigations is inherently nuanced, rich in context, and heavily laden with Protected Health Information (PHI). Standard consumer-grade AI models pose significant data privacy risks and offer little assurance against hallucinations or premature diagnoses. In epidemiology, erroneous outputs or misinterpretations can lead to misallocated resources, flawed outbreak responses, and the erosion of public trust.

### The Arclight Solution: On-Device AI for Frontline Response

To address these unique challenges, the Arclight model architecture provides a targeted, secure solution designed explicitly for edge environments. Arclight models are fully self-contained, allowing them to run locally on mobile or handheld edge devices without external network dependencies. This design eliminates infrastructure setup overhead, API cost vulnerabilities, and cloud-based data privacy risks entirely.

Despite their compact footprint, Arclight models excel at ingesting and structuring unstructured field data—ranging from narrative text and image documentation to voice notes. Output formatting remains tightly controlled and highly structured, ensuring reliability and accuracy when field teams need it most.

## Driving Impact Through FEBE

To showcase the practical application of this approach, the Field Epidemiology, By Epidemiologists (FEBE) project serves as an open-source proof of concept built on the Arclight architecture. Arclight-FEBE demonstrates how specialized, localized AI tools can empower frontline public health workers without compromising security or operational independence.

By delivering an accessible, open-source framework, FEBE offers academic institutions and research organizations a solid foundation to build, adapt, and deploy targeted epidemiological tools worldwide. Ultimately, Arclight-FEBE illustrates how edge-native AI can address critical public health gaps, ensuring that field responders are equipped to navigate an uncertain and challenging future.
